record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on S^{m-1} is determined by heredity coefficients P_{ij,k} satisfying P_{ij,k} >= 0, P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k}, and sum_k P_{ij,k} = 1, via x'_k = sum_{i,j} P_{ij,k} x_i x_j. For Volterra QSOs, transversality means that the associated skew-symmetric matrix A has all even-order leading principal minors nonzero. How should transversality be defined for an arbitrary QSO, and what necessary and sufficient conditions on the full heredity-coefficient tensor P = (P_{ij,k}) characterize arbitrary QSOs that are transversal under that definition?

evidence.quote: A skew-symmetric matrix A is called transversal if all even order leading (principal) minors are nonzero. A Volterra QSO V is called transversal if the corresponding skew-symmetric matrix A is transversal [14],[18],[36].
Problem 2. Define concept of transversality for arbitrary QSO and find necessary and sufficient condition on matrix P = (Pij,k ) of a QSO under which the QSO is a transversal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m : x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ is a mapping of the form
$$x'_k=(Vx)_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the heredity coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy
$$P_{ij,k}\ge 0,\quad P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k},\quad \sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1\ \ \text{for all }i,j.$$

A QSO is called Volterra if $P_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$; in this case the operator can be written as
$$(Vx)_k=x_k\Big(1+\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ki} x_i\Big),$$
with a skew-symmetric matrix $A=(a_{ki})$ satisfying $a_{ki}=-a_{ik}$, $|a_{ki}|\le 1$. A skew-symmetric matrix $A$ is called transversal if all of its even-order leading principal minors are nonzero, and a Volterra QSO is called transversal when its associated $A$ is transversal.

Problem. Formulate a definition of transversality for an arbitrary (not necessarily Volterra) QSO, expressed in terms of the heredity tensor $P=(P_{ij,k})$, that reduces to the above notion in the Volterra case. Then determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the tensor $P$ that characterize when an arbitrary QSO is transversal under the proposed definition.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was located. The problem is posed as an open problem in the survey on quadratic stochastic operators, and existing literature on QSOs (including studies of Volterra, F-, and permutation-type QSOs) does not appear to provide a definition of transversality for arbitrary QSOs together with necessary and sufficient conditions on the heredity tensor.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of QSOs, including Volterra and non-Volterra classes; transversality is discussed only in the Volterra setting via the skew-symmetric matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references address transversality only for Volterra QSOs, indicating the general case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: F-quadratic stochastic operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies subclasses of QSOs beyond Volterra without defining transversality for arbitrary QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: No general transversality criterion for arbitrary QSOs is given in this line of work.
